title: Gallery entry still appears live despite metadata.yaml deletion
description:
metadata.yaml was deleted in e64c746 (2026-03-12) to delist this template from the GTM Community Template Gallery. As of 2026-07-29 the gallery entry at https://tagmanager.google.com/gallery/#/owners/axeptio/templates/GTM_consent_mode_template still appears reachable, and still exposes the dead documentation link that issue #1 reported (support.axeptio.eu/hc/en-gb/articles/9263604989457 -> 404).

Deliberately NOT acted on: restoring metadata.yaml would re-arm the full gallery contract and walk back a deliberate delisting decision.

If a stale public listing for a deprecated template becomes a problem, the route is to chase Google for removal via the gallery submission process, not to change this repo. Issue #1 has been answered and closed pointing users at the Axeptio CMP template.
notes:
CONFIRMED STILL LISTED (verified in browser 2026-08-05).

Gallery entry https://tagmanager.google.com/gallery/#/owners/axeptio/templates/GTM_consent_mode_template renders a live, INSTALLABLE template: 'Axeptio Consent Mode v2 by axeptio', with a working 'Add to workspace' button. Its Documentation link is still the dead https://support.axeptio.eu/hc/en-gb/articles/9263604989457 (the 404 from issue #1).

The status page (/gallery/#/template/axeptio/GTM_consent_mode_template/status) explains why:
  Current Status: Available
  Current Version: 8b2237f7bd52ebe7e37f6b350b8f5e411949e0fb
  Sync log (newest first):
    - 'The metadata.yaml file was not found.'   <- Google DID detect the deletion
    - 'master - GitHub returned an error'
    - several earlier 'Success' entries

So Google detected the missing metadata.yaml and simply FAILED THE SYNC, keeping the last known good version (8b2237f7, Feb 2025) permanently Available. It did not delist.

This contradicts developers.google.com/tag-platform/tag-manager/templates/gallery, which states that deleting either LICENSE or metadata.yaml removes the template automatically. It also invalidates the claim in this repo's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md that deleting metadata.yaml is 'the sanctioned way to remove a template from the gallery' — it stops updates, it does not unlist.

Consequence: everything released here (v1.0.0, v1.0.1) never reaches gallery users; they get the Feb-2025 commit. New users can still install the deprecated template today.

Archiving the repo will NOT unlist it, and archiving FIRST would block every remaining lever (read-only). Whatever fix is chosen must land before archiving.

title: Decide whether to archive the GitHub repository
description:
README declares the template deprecated and unmaintained, and metadata.yaml was deleted to delist it from the GTM gallery, but the repo is not archived on GitHub.

Archiving makes the repo read-only, which FREEZES the release/commitlint/gallery workflows added in the release-automation PR — no further releases, no CI. So this is a deliberate end-state decision, not hygiene.

Decide: archive now (accepting no further changes), or keep it open so security/doc fixes can still ship through the pipeline.
close_reason: Decided: archive the repo and unlist the template (2026-08-05). This closes the open question — archiving freezes the release/commitlint/gallery workflows installed in PR #3, which is the accepted cost of ending the repo's life. master is left coherent at v1.0.1 with a README pointing at axeptio/axeptio-gtm-public-template. Reversible via 'gh repo unarchive' if ever needed.

title: Review whether the stale bot belongs on this deprecated repo
description:
axeptio-bot marked issue #1 as 'stale due to 30 days of inactivity' on 2026-07-29 — a valid bug report that had gone unanswered for ~2.5 years (opened 2024-02-29). Marking a genuine unanswered report as stale is the worst possible response: it looks like the project is triaging when nobody ever read it.

The reply posted to issue #1 explicitly disowns that bot comment.

Decide whether a stale bot should run on a deprecated repo at all. Options: disable it here, or exempt issues that have never received a human response.
close_reason: Moot. Archiving makes GitHub issues read-only, so the stale bot cannot mark anything on this repo again. The one issue it mishandled (#1) was answered and closed on 2026-07-29, and the reply explicitly disowns the stale comment. If the same bot runs on other Axeptio repos the underlying concern still stands there — not tracked here.

title: Port the validate-gallery.py hardening back to axeptio-gtm-public-template
description:
PR #3 hardened scripts/validate-gallery.py in response to Copilot review:

- check_git_available() preflight so a missing git or a run outside a checkout reports one clear failure instead of a traceback or a screenful of invented violations
- git ls-files return code is checked
- template.tpl is validated as git-tracked, like LICENSE already was

The sibling repo axeptio/axeptio-gtm-public-template has the original copy of this script and still carries all three problems. The two scripts are deliberately kept aligned, so port the hardening there to stop them drifting.

Note the sibling repo ALSO publishes a personal email address in its committed .beads/issues.jsonl owner field, on a public repo — same finding Copilot raised here. Worth fixing in the same pass.
close_reason:
Closed only because this repo is being archived — the work itself is NOT done and does not belong to this repo. Re-file against axeptio/axeptio-gtm-public-template.

Its scripts/validate-gallery.py still has all three bugs fixed here in commit 9bbfed1:
1. git() raises FileNotFoundError when git is not on PATH — traceback instead of a clear failure. Fix: catch OSError, return None, and gate every check behind a check_git_available() preflight.
2. 'git ls-files' return code unchecked — an empty result reads as 'nothing is tracked' and emits a screenful of invented violations (including a misleading LICENSE-casing failure) instead of the one real problem.
3. template.tpl is never checked for being git-tracked, unlike LICENSE, so a locally-untracked template passes validation while it would not ship.

Separately, that repo's committed .beads/issues.jsonl publishes a maintainer's personal email address in the owner field of every issue, on a PUBLIC repo. bd derives owner from git user.email and has no --owner flag, and auto-export clobbers hand-edits, so the fix is at the source: set a repo-local noreply user.email, then delete and recreate the issues. Same finding Copilot raised on PR #3 here, fixed here by rebuilding the branch under a noreply address.

Reference implementation: axeptio/GTM_consent_mode_template @ 9bbfed1 and b1b3171.

title: template.tpl retains GTM gallery placeholders and stray content
description:
Pre-existing issues in template.tpl, all out of scope of the release-automation PR:

- ___INFO___ 'id' is still the boilerplate 'cvt_temp_public_id'
- brand.id is 'brand_dummy' with an empty brand.displayName
- ___INFO___ has no 'categories' key (validate-gallery.py warns in delisted mode, would FAIL if the template were ever re-listed)
- the LABEL template parameter contains a leftover French comment: <!-- TODO doc en anglais -->
- ___TESTS___ is empty (scenarios: [])

Only worth fixing if the template is ever resubmitted to the gallery. If it is not, close as wontfix.
close_reason: Wontfix. Repo archived and template unlisted, so the gallery placeholders (cvt_temp_public_id, brand_dummy), the missing categories, the French TODO and the empty ___TESTS___ block are all frozen as-is. These only mattered for a resubmission, which is no longer on the table.

title: LICENSE appendix still has the unfilled copyright placeholder
description:
LICENSE is the verbatim Apache 2.0 boilerplate; its appendix still reads 'Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]' — Axeptio is never named as copyright holder.

Filling it in is legitimate under the gallery contract (the appendix is part of the Apache 2.0 text), but LICENSE is load-bearing: the gallery delists a template whose licence does not match Apache 2.0 exactly, which is what caused SUP-1008 on the sibling repo. Any edit must keep 'Validate gallery contract' green and should be reviewed by legal.

Pre-existing; deliberately out of scope of the release-automation PR.
close_reason: Wontfix. Repo archived, so LICENSE is frozen with the unfilled 'Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]' appendix. The Apache 2.0 grant is valid regardless, and the template is unlisted, so the gallery constraint that made LICENSE load-bearing no longer applies.
